summary:
Before heading to the Moon or Mars, mission teams rehearse on Earth—yet historically they rely on the same five expensive, remote sites (Atacama, Hawaii, Antarctica) selected primarily because they "look similar" in photos.

We developed PROTOTERRA, an open-source, planetary-scale search engine that quantitatively identifies terrestrial analogs for permanent Moon base candidates (Artemis III polar landing regions) and Mars exploration sites. Using the Yuca Supercomputer at Universidad de Sonora, PROTOTERRA harmonizes elevation and environmental datasets across three worlds into identical 32×32 km patches at 500 m/pixel.

By fusing NASA LOLA, MOLA, MODIS, and EMIT data, PROTOTERRA evaluated over 177,000 planetary and 40,000 Earth terrains, discovering 3,522 uncatalogued candidate sites. Crucially, PROTOTERRA explicitly calculates where the physical analogy breaks (gravity, atmospheric pressure, and cosmic radiation) and delivers real-world travel logistics (distance to roads and airports) to democratize analog research for student teams and emerging space agencies.
details:
PROTOTERRA: Grounded in Earth. Built for Beyond.

LIVE LINKS: • GitHub Repository: https://github.com/OwenSolis03/prototerra • Live Web Application: https://owensolis03.github.io/prototerra/ • Supercomputing Infrastructure: Powered by ACARUS / Yuca Cluster (Universidad de Sonora)

  1. WHAT DOES IT DO AND HOW DOES IT WORK?

PROTOTERRA replaces subjective, visual intuition with high-performance computing to systematically discover terrestrial analog locations for Moon and Mars exploration.

The engine operates on a mathematically unified geomorphometric pipeline:

• Harmonized Scale (32x32 km Patches): Every candidate site on the Moon, Mars, and Earth is projected into a local Azimuthal Equidistant (AEQD) projection at 500 m/pixel. This removes planetary distortion and allows fair topographic comparisons independent of mismatched planetary elevation datums.

• Feature Extraction: Measures slope (mean and 90th percentile), topographic relief, hypsometric integral, detrended elevation roughness, and terrain ruggedness index (TRI).

• Environmental and Aridity Filtering: Moon and Mars lack vegetation; using 12 months of NASA MODIS NDVI data, PROTOTERRA strips vegetated terrain to isolate approximately 40,000 bare-ground candidate patches worldwide.

• NASA Multi-Sensor Fusion: Incorporates daytime and nighttime thermal amplitudes (MODIS LST and Mars THEMIS), lunar polar temperatures and ice stability depths (LRO Diviner PRP), and surface mineralogy (NASA EMIT L3ASA, JAXA Kaguya MI, and MGS TES).

• Dynamic Mission Similarity Index (MSI): Calculates multi-criteria similarity scores across 7 dimensions, instantly re-weighted in a client-side reactive web dashboard for 5 specific engineering presets: Rover Mobility, Base Construction, Geology, Dust Storms, and ISRU Polar Ice Traps.

  1. HOW IS OUR PROJECT CREATIVE AND DIFFERENT?

Most hackathon approaches produce static catalogs of already well-known locations (Atacama, Hawaii, Rio Tinto) or compare visual RGB imagery. PROTOTERRA breaks conventional methods:

• Physics over Pixels: We never compare camera colors. We evaluate real physical terrain metrics and environmental stress.

• Novelty Discovery: Rather than benchmarking known sites, the algorithm discovered 3,522 new uncatalogued candidate sites (representing 96% of all identified matches), including accessible high-fidelity locations in Northwest Mexico (Sonora and Baja California) with over 90% MSI.

• Where the Analogy Breaks: This was a core challenge requirement that other tools omit. For every site, PROTOTERRA explicitly quantifies the physical divergence in real units: gravitational differential (0.38g vs 1g), atmospheric pressure (6.4 hPa CO2 vs 1013 hPa), daily thermal swings, and surface radiation measured by Curiosity's RAD instrument.

  1. WHAT IS THE INTENDED IMPACT AND BENEFITS?

• Democratizing Space Exploration: Antarctic and Atacama analog expeditions cost hundreds of thousands of dollars, excluding Latin American universities, startups, and emerging space organizations. PROTOTERRA empowers researchers worldwide to conduct validated hardware trials close to home at a fraction of the cost.

• Logistical Viability: Every site displays calculated geodesic distances to the nearest operational road and international airport using global Natural Earth infrastructure networks.

• Open University Science: 100% open source, reproducible, and computed on public university supercomputing infrastructure (Yuca, ACARUS / UniSon).

  1. TOOLS, CODING LANGUAGES, HARDWARE, AND SOFTWARE

• Supercomputing and HPC: ACARUS Yuca Cluster (AMD EPYC compute nodes), Linux, Slurm Workload Manager (127 batch jobs executed, approximately 20 CPU core-hours aggregated).

• Core Languages and Data Science: Python 3.11, NumPy, SciPy (cKDTree spatial indexing and RBF kernel matrices), Pandas, PyArrow/Parquet.

• Geospatial and Remote Sensing Stack: GDAL, Rasterio, PyProj, GeoPandas, PyHDF (HDF4 MODIS reader), Xarray, NetCDF.

• Machine Learning: Scikit-Learn (Unsupervised MiniBatchKMeans for planetary terrain archetype clustering).

• Web Application: Vue 3, Vite, TypeScript, Sass, Leaflet GIS mapping, anime.js, KaTeX, highlight.js.
